title.narrative: CONSOLIDAMENTO DEL MILAN URBAN FOOD POLICY PACT (MUFPP) - FASE II
Strengthening of the Milan Urban Food Policy Pact (MUFPP) – phase II

description.narrative: 1) Rafforzamento del Segretariato MUFPP 2) Sviluppo di nuove competenze e strumenti per lo sviluppo di food policy nelle città firmatarie e promozione dell'MUFPP in nuove città ritenute reciprocamente prioritarie 3) Consolidamento dei temi del MUFPP nel dibattito nazionale e internazionale

A seguito dell’implementazione dell’iniziativa 0012739/01/0 “Consolidamento del Milan Urban Food Policy Pact (MUFPP)”, la presente proposta configura una fase II di follow-up volta a rafforzare il MUFPP quale principale piattaforma globale di cooperazione decentrata sulle politiche alimentari urbane. Lanciato dal Comune di Milano come eredità di EXPO 2015, il MUFPP riunisce oggi oltre 330 città firmatarie nel mondo, impegnate nella trasformazione dei sistemi alimentari urbani in chiave sostenibile, inclusiva e resiliente.L’obiettivo generale è contribuire alla promozione delle politiche alimentari urbane, in particolare nei contesti di cooperazione allo sviluppo, in coerenza con il DTPI 2024-2026 e con gli SDGs 2, 11, 12 e 17. L’obiettivo specifico è il rafforzamento della capacità di azione del MUFPP di supportare le città situate nei Paesi partner di AICS, attraverso una più efficace offerta di assistenza tecnica, formazione, scambi tra città e networking, e un più solido posizionamento nei principali fora internazionali.I gruppi target principali sono le amministrazioni locali delle città firmatarie del Patto (e potenziali nuove aderenti), con particolare focus sui Paesi partner della Cooperazione italiana, e i loro funzionari e funzionarie coinvolti nelle politiche alimentari urbane. La logica di intervento si articola su due assi tra loro integrati: i) rafforzamento ed espansione della rete di città MUFPP, attraverso la promozione del Patto e l’accompagnamento all’adesione di nuove città nei Paesi partner, la realizzazione di percorsi strutturati di formazione e accompagnamento tecnico, scambi peer-to-peer, missioni e visite di studio, nonché lo sviluppo di strumenti tecnico?metodologici, pubblicazioni e studi di fattibilità a supporto delle politiche alimentari urbane; ii) posizionamento congiunto MUFPP?AICS nei principali fora, network e piattaforme internazionali sui sistemi alimentari, con particolare attenzione alla valorizzazione delle esperienze delle città dei Paesi partner e alla capitalizzazione dei risultati in prodotti di policy e di conoscenza. L’iniziativa, della durata di 36 mesi e dal valore complessivo di 600.000,00 euro, è attuata tramite Convenzione con il Comune di Milano, in continuità con la fase I. Essa risponde all’esigenza di AICS di consolidare un approccio urbano alla cooperazione allo sviluppo e riconosce nel MUFPP uno strumento privilegiato per la localizzazione degli SDGs a livello urbano, valorizzando al contempo il ruolo di AICS quale partner strategico per l’estensione e la qualificazione della rete nei contesti di cooperazione.

Following the implementation of initiative 0012739/01/0 “Consolidation of the Milan Urban Food Policy Pact (MUFPP)”, this proposal constitutes a Phase II follow-up aimed at further strengthening the MUFPP as the main global platform for decentralized cooperation on urban food policies. Launched by the City of Milan as a legacy of EXPO 2015, the MUFPP currently brings together over 330 signatory cities worldwide, all committed to transforming urban food systems in a sustainable, inclusive and resilient way.The overall objective is to contribute to the promotion of urban food policies, particularly in development cooperation contexts, in line with the 2024-2026 DTPI and SDGs 2, 11, 12 and 17. The specific objective is to strengthen the MUFPP’s capacity to support cities located in partner countries, through a more effective offer of technical assistance, training, city-to-city exchanges and networking, and stronger joint positioning in key international fora.The main target groups are local administrations of signatory cities (and potential new members), with a specific focus on partner countries and their officials involved in urban food policies.The intervention logic is structured around two mutually reinforcing axes: (i) strengthening and expansion of the MUFPP city network, through promotion of the Pact and support to the adhesion of new cities in partner countries, the implementation of structured training and technical assistance programmes, peer-to-peer exchanges, missions and study visits, as well as the development of technical and methodological tools, publications and feasibility studies to support urban food policies; and (ii) joint positioning of MUFPP and AICS in key international fora, networks and platforms on food systems, with particular attention to showcasing the experiences of cities in partner countries and capitalizing on results through policy and knowledge products.The initiative, lasting 36 months and with a total AICS contribution of EUR 600,000, is implemented through an Agreement with the City of Milan, in continuity with Phase I. It responds to AICS’s need to consolidate an urban approach within its development cooperation strategies and recognizes the MUFPP as a key instrument for the localization of the SDGs at city level, while at the same time acknowledging AICS as a strategic partner for expanding and qualifying the MUFPP network in cooperation contexts.

tag.narrative: By 2020, substantially increase the number of cities and human settlements adopting and implementing integrated policies and plans towards inclusion, resource efficiency, mitigation and adaptation to climate change, resilience to disasters, and develop and implement, in line with the Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction 2015–2030, holistic disaster risk management at all levels
By 2030, end hunger and ensure access by all people, in particular the poor and people in vulnerable situations, including infants, to safe, nutritious and sufficient food all year round
By 2030, halve per capita global food waste at the retail and consumer levels and reduce food losses along production and supply chains, including post-harvest losses
Develop effective, accountable and transparent institutions at all levels
Encourage and promote effective public, public-private and civil society partnerships, building on the experience and resourcing strategies of partnerships
End hunger, achieve food security and improved nutrition and promote sustainable agriculture

Enhance North-South, South-South and triangular regional and international cooperation on and access to science, technology and innovation and enhance knowledge-sharing on mutually agreed terms, including through improved coordination among existing mechanisms, in particular at the United Nations level, and through a global technology facilitation mechanism

Enhance international support for implementing effective and targeted capacity-building in developing countries to support national plans to implement all the Sustainable Development Goals, including through North-South, South-South and triangular cooperation
Ensure sustainable consumption and production patterns
Make cities and human settlements inclusive, safe, resilient and sustainable
Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels
Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
Support positive economic, social and environmental links between urban, peri-urban and rural areas by strengthening national and regional development planning
